name: Check-first model (residents-only)
task: In an outage event, rank the areas of the region by how many hours each will stay dark, so that crews and neighbors check the longest-dark areas first.
method: LightGBM regression on log1p(dark hours), 200 trees, 7 leaves, at least 200 rows per leaf; one row per area per event; inputs known at the event start

inputs.name: out_prev1h
inputs.plain: Homes reporting no power in the area, 1 hour before the event start
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Number of homes in the section that reported no power in the last hour

inputs.name: out_max_prev6h
inputs.plain: Most homes reporting no power in the area, in the 6 hours before the event start
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Largest number of homes in the section that reported no power in the last 6 hours

inputs.name: month
inputs.plain: Month of the event start
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Month on the Hollow calendar

inputs.hollowEquivalent: Mean length of earlier blackouts in the district

inputs.hollowEquivalent: Hours since the district's last blackout ended

inputs.hollowEquivalent: Number of homes in the section (count of rooms)

inputs.hollowEquivalent: Head count of the section

inputs.name: svi
inputs.plain: CDC Social Vulnerability Index, overall percentile (2010)
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Depth and vulnerability of the section's level

inputs.name: svi_t1
inputs.plain: SVI theme 1: income, jobs and education
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Vulnerability of the level: income and work

inputs.plain: SVI theme 2: age, disability and single parents

inputs.name: svi_t3
inputs.plain: SVI theme 3: minority status and language
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Vulnerability of the level: language and minority status

inputs.name: svi_t4
inputs.plain: SVI theme 4: housing type and transport
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Vulnerability of the level: crowded housing and access

inputs.name: utilities
inputs.plain: Number of electric utilities that serve the area
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Number of repair crews that serve the section

inputs.name: ba_is_*
inputs.plain: Which region the area belongs to (one 0/1 column per training region, 36 regions)
inputs.hollowEquivalent: Which district the section belongs to

excluded: Weather at the event start (temperature, dew point, pressure, wind, rain, 24 h extremes): residents of the Hollow have no weather.
Weather forecasts: residents have no forecast.

Grid-operator data from EIA-930 (demand against the day-ahead forecast and against the 30-day peak, share of power imported, share from gas, 6 h changes in generation): the Directorate does not give residents grid figures.

HHS emPOWER (people on powered medical equipment): our copy is a 2026 snapshot, so it was not known before the 2015-2024 events. It is a fair Hollow input (residents can report it), but it cannot be tested on this history.

periods.train: July 2015 to December 2020 (events that ended before 2021)
periods.test: 2023 to 2024 (scored once, after every choice was frozen)

example.event: Hurricane Beryl, Texas (ERCOT region, 188 counties, 49 went dark). The model's top 10 held 7 of the 10 longest-dark counties; the history baseline held 2.

limits: 95% intervals on FINAL TEST (2,000 bootstrap resamples of events): within-event Spearman 0.285 to 0.347 (history 0.183 to 0.254); top-10 overlap 0.421 to 0.494 (history 0.243 to 0.316).
The model ranks areas. Its hour values are much too low in large events (in Hurricane Beryl, Brazoria County: 4.1 h predicted, 165 h actual). Use the order, not the hours.
Predicting 0 hours everywhere has a lower mean error (2.00 h) than the model (2.27 h), because most areas have no dark hour. The error metric does not measure the ranking.

The data is real US outages (EAGLE-I county outage reports, 2015-2024). The Hollow inputs are stand-ins: reported outages for residents' reports, CDC SVI for depth, counties for sections, balancing-authority regions for districts.
Month and hour may carry storm-season information. The Hollow has no storms, so part of what the model learned from the calendar may not carry over.

Events are defined from outage reports (at least a set share of the region's customers out). The model does not predict whether an event starts, only which areas stay dark longest once it has started.

In Hurricane Beryl the model missed Harris County, the longest-dark county (176 h): the outage reports showed only 214 of about 1.8 million customers out 1 hour before the event start, so the model predicted 0 h. The model is only as good as the residents' reports.
Removing weather and grid inputs did not lower the score: those inputs have one value per event, so they cannot rank areas inside one event by themselves.

source.label: EAGLE-I county outages (ORNL), CDC SVI, Census, EIA-861
